referents.why: Second person singular masculine. The speech is Moses' speech to Pharaoh (the Exo.8.5 frame: he said Moses to Pharaoh), so the addressee is Pharaoh, the only masculine singular addressee.
Possessive second person singular masculine, in the same speech to Pharaoh; your houses are Pharaoh's houses.
Possessive second person singular masculine, in the same speech to Pharaoh; your officials are Pharaoh's officials.
Possessive second person singular masculine, in the same speech to Pharaoh; your people are Pharaoh's people.
Third person feminine plural agrees with frogs (w3, feminine plural), the subject of cl0. The frogs remain only in the Nile.
referents.category: third person agreeing with the subject of the prior clause

links.why: The builder id cl4 names no clause of this verse, which has only cl0 and cl1. Read as a clause of an earlier verse it is cross-verse, and then is within-verse only. The sense is not a next event: the departure is the outcome the prayer is to bring about, which the result link below records.
The command pray to Yahweh (Exo.8.4#cl2) is followed by waw and a third person weqatal, they will depart. The prayer is to bring about the frogs leaving, so cl0 is what the command brings about.
links.category: command and its outcome across verses

groups.why: Moses speaking to Pharaoh, with no frame clause in this verse; both clauses continue his speech. If the speech that begins at Exo.8.6#turn1 runs on into this verse, this group should be merged into that turn instead.
groups.category: speech continued without a new frame

none_fit.what: A restriction: the frogs depart from them, but remain in the Nile. The text has no but or except, and the but_rather type needs a negated clause before it.
